handlers.ts.label: bad
handlers.ts.reason: failure mode: five handle* return Promise<Result<T>> and report failure with err(); handleArchive returns Promise<Note> and throws for the same not-found case.

project_files.ts.label: bad
project_files.ts.reason: async-ness: four read* are async over fs/promises; readSchema does the same file read synchronously with readFileSync and no reason given.

commands.ts.label: bad
commands.ts.reason: parameter order: four commands take (ctx, input); runExport takes (input, ctx) for the same kind of work.

parsers.ts.label: bad
parsers.ts.reason: failure mode: four parse* return T | null on bad input; parseVersion does the same regex parse and throws instead.

fetchers.ts.label: bad
fetchers.ts.reason: failure mode: four fetch* throw on !res.ok and return Promise<T>; fetchPlan returns Promise<Result<Plan>> with err() for the same GET.

formatters.ts.label: bad
formatters.ts.reason: async-ness: four pure Intl formatters are plain functions returning string; formatMoney is async and returns Promise<string> for the same pure formatting.

session_events.ts.label: bad
session_events.ts.reason: async-ness: four on* handlers are async and await audit.write and metrics.increment; onLogout does the same two calls without await and returns void.

serializers.ts.label: bad
serializers.ts.reason: parameter order: four write* take (out, value); writeDate takes (value, out) for the same kind of encode-and-push.

worker_routes.ts.label: bad
worker_routes.ts.reason: parameter order: four handle* take (env, request); handleCancelJob takes (request, env) for the same kind of route handler.

auth_routes.ts.label: clean
auth_routes.ts.reason: hard clean: one odd item, but only in its name (handleSignup among *Handler); all five share (req, res) => Promise<void>. Naming is module-naming-consistent's subject.

notifications.ts.label: clean
notifications.ts.reason: hard clean: one odd item, but only in its name (dispatchPush among send*); all four share (n) => Promise<DeliveryReceipt>. Naming is module-naming-consistent's subject.

lookups.ts.label: clean
lookups.ts.reason: hard clean: one odd item, but only in its name (loadInvoice among get*); all five share (db, id) => Promise<T | null>. Naming is module-naming-consistent's subject.

permissions.ts.label: clean
permissions.ts.reason: hard clean: one odd item, but only in its name (checkAdmin among is/has/can); all five are (session, ...) => boolean. Naming is module-naming-consistent's subject.

user_repository.ts.label: clean
user_repository.ts.reason: clean: four verbs for one operation, but every signature has the same shape (db, id) => Promise<T | null>; nothing at the signature level deviates.

factories.ts.label: clean
factories.ts.reason: clean: four constructor verbs, identical signature shape (plain, returns the record); no signature deviant.

settings.ts.label: clean
settings.ts.reason: clean: five setter verbs, identical signature shape (settings, value) => Settings; no signature deviant.

product_source.ts.label: clean
product_source.ts.reason: hard clean: getProduct is the only sync item, but it reads a cache while its siblings hit the network -- the difference follows from the operation.

codec.ts.label: clean
codec.ts.reason: hard clean: two groups (frame codec, header codec), each internally consistent; no single deviant.

rate_limiter.ts.label: clean
rate_limiter.ts.reason: hard clean: one public item; nothing to deviate from.

order_service.ts.label: clean
order_service.ts.reason: hard clean: cancelOrder returns void and getOrder throws where find/list return arrays, but each does a different operation; no one item breaks a shared shape.

validators.ts.label: clean
validators.ts.reason: hard clean: fail() has a different shape from the five validate* items, but it is the helper every one of them calls.

sync.ts.label: clean
sync.ts.reason: hard clean: two groups of three, each internally consistent (three sync diff* over (local, remote), three async push*); no single deviant. The closest clean (0.48): pushSnapshot takes (remote, local) where its two push siblings take (remote, changes), a different parameter, not a reordering.

jobs.ts.label: clean
jobs.ts.reason: hard clean: noopJob is the only sync item, and the comment above it says why -- a deliberate, documented exception.

middleware.ts.label: clean
middleware.ts.reason: hard clean: compose(...stack) differs in shape from the five (req, res, next) middlewares, but it is a combinator over them.

preferences.ts.label: clean
preferences.ts.reason: hard clean: two groups (async load/save on a path; sync get/set on the object) plus resetPreferences, a factory for the default; no single deviant.

accounts.ts.label: clean
accounts.ts.reason: hard clean: getAccountOrThrow throws where four find* return T | null, but its name states the different failure mode and it is built on findAccount.

uploads.ts.label: clean
uploads.ts.reason: hard clean: putExport takes an extra optional opts parameter; the shared (bucket, key, body) => Promise<void> shape is intact.
